“Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low.” In the Phillips curve and expectations-augmented frameworks, tight labor markets can raise inflation pressure, but anchored expectations and sticky-information dynamics (e.g., Mankiw and Reis, 2002) imply a muted, gradual pass-through. The Committee’s emphasis on a symmetric 2 percent target and “further gradual” rate hikes is consistent with Taylor principle/rule guidance and credibility-preserving gradualism; the observation that market-based inflation compensation remains low signals that inflation expectations are well anchored, a hallmark of effective inflation targeting. Strong business fixed investment supports real activity, in line with standard investment–output links in macro-finance, while the policy stance remaining accommodative suggests ongoing support for demand with careful monitoring of inflation expectations. Net tone: cautiously optimistic and data-dependent rather than exuberant.
